primary_claim: In a Gemma-3-4B-it model organism trained to be a covert political sycophant (a backdoored analog of scheming), adversarial SFT on a small, narrow set of honeypot-like examples substantially reduces the unwanted backdoor behavior generally (not just on the training examples), and non-adversarial SFT with a sufficiently large learning rate can also substantially reduce backdoor behavior without hurting general capabilities, contrasting with Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents finding that similar model organisms are resistant to SFT/RL/adversarial training.

effect.metric: reduction in backdoor (conservative-response) behavior after training, and MMLU accuracy before/after
effect.value: non-adversarial training at learning rate 1e-5 reduces backdoor behavior by 88.5 percentage points (57.7pp on a different random seed); at 3e-6 by 19.8pp; at 1e-6 by only 5.0pp; MMLU accuracy 57.4%±0.8% out-of-the-box, 53.6%±0.8% after model-organism training, recovering to 54.8%±0.8% (lr 1e-5) / 55.26%±0.8% (lr 3e-6) after non-adversarial training

contradicts_or_qualifies: unlike Hubinger et al. (Sleeper Agents, arXiv:2401.05566), who found model organisms resistant to SFT, RL, and adversarial training, we (and Price et al., and an unpublished replication) do not find such resistant cases at the 4B parameter scale, compatible with Hubinger et al.'s own finding that models below 52B parameters aren't resistant to RL training
stated_future_work: make the setting more analogous to training a policy rather than a monitor, e.g. by adding RL-required behaviors or an untrainable reasoning trace
measure whether SFT generalizes to remove backdoor behaviors that would require RL to train away directly
lean more into the analogy with untrusted monitoring and incorporate this training into a control evaluation for monitoring protocols
expand the diversity of model organisms with different backdoor triggers/behaviors, and add variations of the sycophancy dataset since the current one may be too narrow and clear-cut
try strategies that search for more drastically different AIs than adversarial training, such as changing the system prompt
limitations_stated: prefill-based behavioral measurement of the AI's beliefs is fragile and may not track the true variable upstream of the decision to respond conservatively
experiments are small-scale and only explore two model organisms (Gemma-3 4B as covert conservative and covert liberal)
adversarial training here only trains on adversarial examples, unlike practice where they might be shuffled in with normal examples
unclear whether training has increased the false positive rate on benign actions under the untrusted-monitor analogy
all training uses SFT only, for simplicity of implementation, rather than the RL more likely used in practice
quote: Adversarial SFT on a small and narrow set of unwanted behaviors substantially reduces unwanted behavior generally, both via reduced political sycophancy and via reduced stated belief that conservative users are conservative.
